survivors.crates/genui-core/src/validate/increment: Equivalent for every cache produced by validation. Any Bind in the dirty set whose kind differs from classify is already rejected in the change loop by the `cached.kinds.get(&s.name) != kind` check (line 190), and an unchanged cached statement classifies to its cached kind. The only other table sources are queries: the parser requires a query value to be a `tool(...)` call, which classify maps to Kind::Value, and query entries are inserted with Kind::Value (line 133). States live in state_sources, not table. Thus for every dirty name with a table source the final kind-mismatch test is false whether the source kind is Bind or not, so flipping the equality cannot select the fallback.
Equivalent: the extra rotation only changes behaviour when `height(left.right) == height(left.left)`. With that equality the double rotation `rotate_left(left)` followed by `rotate_right(self)` produces exactly the same tree shape and heights as the single `rotate_right(self)` (the two-step rotation of a balanced three-node left spine is the same AVL rebalance). In-order and pre-order keys, cached summaries and all visit results are unchanged; only an extra local clone/rotation runs.

Equivalent: symmetric to 131:40. When `height(right.left) == height(right.right)`, `rotate_right(right)` followed by `rotate_left(self)` yields the same shape and heights as the single `rotate_left(self)`, so tree contents, summaries, ranges and visit output are identical.

Equivalent: this guard only decides whether to skip a subtree whose summary has no materialized work. Replacing `used > 0` by the always-true `used >= 0` can only make the guard enter more often. Every actual visit is still gated by the item-level predicate at line 317, which keeps `used > 0`, and a summary with `used == 0` has no descendant item with used > 0 by construction of the summary. No extra key is emitted; only traversal work changes.

Equivalent: same summary guard, for effects. `effects >= 0` is always true, so it can only traverse subtrees that the original skipped. Any emitted effect is still gated by the item-level `profile.effects > 0` predicate at line 317, and a summary with `effects == 0` contains no descendant work, so the visit sequence and results are unchanged.

Equivalent: this is only the left-child traversal test. Changing `key > after` to `key >= after` enters the left subtree when `key == after`. Every key in that left subtree is strictly less than `key`, hence strictly less than `after`, so both this traversal test and the item-level exclusive `after` test at line 313 still reject them. No extra item is visited and the range semantics stay exclusive.

Equivalent: this is only the right-child traversal test. Changing `key < until` to `key <= until` enters the right subtree when `key == until`. Every key in that right subtree is strictly greater than `key`, hence strictly greater than `until`, so the item-level inclusive `key <= until` test at line 314 still rejects all of them. The emitted key set and result order are unchanged.
